name: Truth Sleuth (Wisconsin Watch × Center for Media Engagement)
what: Crowdsourced misinformation reporting tool with a newsroom fact-checking dashboard, built with UT-Austin's Center for Media Engagement.
pitch: It is multi-newsroom by design — submitters pick which agency receives the report — so WPR could join rather than build, and OEC could route flags into Watch Ledger entries.
access: Built — Wisconsin Watch — free (free reader account to submit; joining as an agency requires contacting Wisconsin Watch/CME)

name: ICE arrests in Wisconsin tracker (news app)
what: Standing news app tracking Wisconsin ICE arrests, framed as 'follow what happens next' rather than a one-off story.
pitch: Same-state peer turning a spike story into a permanent tracker off Wisconsin records WPR can also reach — the exact Ledger pattern, on a beat WPR has no archive for.

name: Beacon Documenters training cohort
what: Second training class put 48 residents from 33 ZIP codes into local government meetings as note-takers.
pitch: Gavel automates meeting summaries but cannot put humans in rooms; the Beacon shows the recruiting and training pipeline — 89 trained since November 2025 — that would give Gavel verified human notes.
access: Audience — The Beacon (Kansas City) — free to read; Documenters-network model, paid stipends to participants

name: VTDigger 2026 General Election Guide
what: Single election guide product combining candidate and race pages, campaign finance data and voting resources.
pitch: WPR already ships results and voter guide tools, but not campaign finance. VTDigger bundles all three under one URL — a concrete gap to close before November.

name: Ask Wisconsin Watch: reader-submitted candidate questions
what: Call-out asking readers to supply the questions the newsroom puts to 2026 candidates.
pitch: A Wisconsin peer is sourcing voter guide content from readers on the same ballot WPR covers, which makes both the questions and the answers shareable.

name: Beacon community survey published as a story
what: The Beacon published its audience survey findings, reporting readers most want money and spending coverage.
pitch: Publishing survey results as a story, not an internal memo, is free trust-building — and it validates that spending accountability, WPR's Settlement and Rent Ledgers, is what readers actually ask for.

name: Sahan Journal × Mixed Blood Theatre housing story call-out
what: Newsroom partners with a theater to collect residents' housing stories for a live community event.
pitch: Rent Ledger holds filings but not testimony. An arts-venue partner supplies a room, an audience and a reason for tenants to talk — cheap reach beyond existing WPR readers.

name: NNS intergenerational dialogues on violence
what: Wisconsin newsroom ran facilitated community dialogues as a reporting method and published the lessons.
pitch: A Wisconsin peer treating convening as reporting, with the method written up. Care Ledger beats — caregiving, crisis response — need exactly this lived-experience layer that records cannot supply.

name: Bridge Michigan executive editor for growth and audience strategy
what: Bridge created a senior editor role explicitly scoped to growth and audience strategy.
pitch: A structural signal, not a routine replacement: growth lives inside the editing chain rather than in marketing. Useful precedent for how WPR scopes whoever owns the newsletter pipeline and jobs board.
